pixel_description: Render-only: outdoor photo of hand truck tilted back on concrete stairs carrying a taped cardboard box. Twin parallel silver tubes form the spine from top to base, joined by two small cross plates and telescopic collars near top. Top ends bend back into a handle with two black rubber grips, brake lever under right grip. Bottom ends bolt to a bulky dark grey cast housing. A small side crank with black knob protrudes from the housing. Critical part tri-star wheel cluster: centered on that housing/axle, made of dark metal star arms ending in black solid rubber wheels with silver hubs. Five wheels resolved: three on left in clear triangular 120-deg arrangement - one touching the vertical riser, one on upper tread, one rearward - plus two on near/right side - one sitting on lower tread nose under the toe, one partly hidden behind frame. Arms converge to common transverse axle bolted to spine base. Light wood-colored toe plate L-bolted to spine base brackets sits under box bottom and touches lower step edge. Box sits on toe, leans against spine tubes. Two black fabric straps wrap box in X-cross. Wheels physically touch stair concrete at two noses, toe touches box and step, housing touches spine and star arms, star arms touch wheels, spine touches handle via collars.

deviations.measured: 1 distinct hub segmented, 2 side clusters seen by eye
deviations.why: 3/4 view merges the two mirrored side clusters onto one central housing. Five rubber wheels in triangular star arrangement are resolved, the sixth hidden behind frame/toe. Tri-star triangle and central axle preserved, so this is occlusion/segmentation, not missing function.

deviations.measured: not segmented as 'metal box' but bulky dark cast housing visible
deviations.why: Label mismatch. Dark bolted housing at spine base with side crank knob sits exactly on cluster axle to spine load path, matching self-locking worm plus pawl location. Function intact.

deviations.measured: 2 silver tubes seen but segmented as 1; 7.7x segmented handle length
deviations.why: Segmenter merged the twin tubes and measured only the black grip as handle. By eye twin parallel aluminium tubes with cross-braces and telescopic collars run full length ~1000-1200mm, similar to full handle loop length. Carry function unchanged.

deviations.measured: not segmented as 'foot plate' but light plate visible under box
deviations.why: Label/shape mismatch. Light wooden/metal plate under cardboard box bolted to spine base brackets, supporting parcel weight. Hinge line implied. Present and loaded correctly.

deviations.expected: vertical long axis, about 0.9x spine length
deviations.why: Perspective and partial measurement. Spine is inclined ~45deg on stairs, handle loop continues then bends back with near-horizontal grips for two-hand push. Segmenter measured only short grip, not full telescopic closed-loop tubes which are ~900-1100mm with spine. Relative orientation follows spine as in OPEN L sketch, brake lever under right grip visible.
Two black polyester bands crossing in X around box merged in segmentation. Both secure parcel to frame/toe. Count difference is merging, not missing securement.

Side-view expectation vs 3/4 photo showing both left and right clusters. Three left wheels form 120-deg triangle, two right wheels show second cluster, sixth occluded behind housing. Total 6 implied, solid black rubber with hubs. Extra visibility is viewpoint, not extra parts; stair-nose contact on two noses preserved.

12-30mm quick pins/skid pads too small to segment at this distance. Bolts/rivets visible on spine-tube joints, telescopic collars and toe hinge brackets provide lock points. Absence in segmentation is resolution, not missing fold-lock function.

s1_differences: No structural difference. Same parts, same connections, same relative sizes and directions allowing for 3/4 photo perspective vs abstract node diagram: twin-tube spine to toe hinge to parcel, spine to telescopic closed-loop handle with brake lever, cluster axle to worm housing with crank to spine, wheels on cluster arms contacting two stair noses, straps securing parcel.
s2_feedback: No design flaw exposed. Load path handle-spine-worm-cluster-stairs is continuous, toe clears stair nose and supports box, five of six wheels show rolling/climbing contact without interference, crank and brake lever are reachable and separate from parcel, frame shows no buckling or impossible assembly.
notes: Photorealistic render with no overlaid text/diagram. Segmenter misses are label, merging and occlusion effects. Human inspection confirms twin tubes, worm housing with crank, two tri-star side sets, toe plate, closed-loop handle with dead-man lever, X straps, bolts at joints.
